articles.title: Air Force officer killed in rappelling accident before UTSA’s game against Navy
articles.summary: Officer fell from rafters during pregame display. Man treated on field before being taken to hospital. An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game against Navy on Saturday.
body: The officer, who has not been named, was taking part in an event to celebrate UTSA’s Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans night. He fell on to the field while rappelling down from the stadium rafters. He was treated on the field before being taken away on a stretcher. He later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Nellis Air Force Base said he was part of the 6th Combat Training Squadron. The unit helps train military members to rappel down from helicopters.
In video of the incident, the crowd could be heard reacting when the officer fell to the field. The Alamodome roof is around 170ft above the field.

“There was something – you could just tell that the energy was just gone [from the crowd],” UTSA coach Jeff Traylor said after the game. “I’ve never had to deal with anything like that before. It just puts things in perspective. It really does.”
The start of the game was delayed for around 10 minutes after the incident.

articles.title: Kartal denied biggest win of career after Chwalinska fightback in Wuhan Open final
articles.summary: French Open finalist wins 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 for her first title. Kartal will become new British No 1 after record run. Sonay Kartal missed out on winning the biggest title of her career as her brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a final defeat by Maja Chwalinska.
body: Kartal has enjoyed her best tournament only a fortnight after returning from six months out with a back injury, but her efforts appeared to catch up with her as she faded in a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 loss.

Instead it was Chwalinska who lifted her first WTA 1000 trophy – the first of her career at any level on the WTA Tour – after fighting back from a set and a break down. The 25-year-old made a stunning breakthrough earlier this season when she reached the French Open final as a qualifier, and she will now move to the brink of the top 10.

At 170 in the world, Kartal was the lowest-ranked player to reach a final at this level since the format was introduced in 2009 and only the second British woman after Johanna Konta. She fell short of matching Konta, who won the Miami Open in 2017, but Kartal’s reward will be a new ranking of 50, making her the British No 1 for the first time.

Kartal, whose only tour title came at a small event in Tunisia in 2024, continued the form she had shown throughout the tournament in the opening set, immediately breaking the relatively weak Chwalinska serve.

articles.title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again
articles.summary: Two goals each from a rampant ­Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.
body: It was a thrilling show and a statement from the home team, a game laden with stunning goals after a frustrating first half that allowed Tottenham more of the ball than Chelsea would have been happy with.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg’s first-half equaliser, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano powered in the fourth and fifth before Signe Gaupset pulled one back and Carpenter converted for the second time.

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat to London City Lionesses Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. Spurs looked lightweight against the Bromley-based side, despite going into the game unbeaten.

At Stamford Bridge heads were up and it had looked like it would be a different story after a strong start by the visiting team. The concession of the opening goal in the 25th minute was a cruel reminder of their defensive issues. It was Toko Koga who was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender turned her back on James, who dispossessed her and drove towards the near post before she fired in at the far post from the tightest of angles.

articles.title: What awaits Everton hero Ferguson in shock Glens role?
articles.summary: The expected appointment of former Scotland striker Duncan Ferguson at Glentoran will be one of the most surprising in Irish Premiership history.
body: With the appointment of Duncan Ferguson at the Oval expected to be confirmed on Monday, the club's five-week search for a new manager illustrates again that there is the easy way, the hard way, and the Glentoran way.
When the east Belfast outfit parted company with Declan Devine on 14 September, the simple solution to the early-season vacancy appeared to be a reunion with former assistant Tiernan Lynch.
A two-time winner of the Irish Premiership with Larne, Lynch was freshly back on the market after leaving Derry City in August and immediately installed as favourite for the post.
Instead, the Glens made the trickier prospect of prying Jim Magilton out of his contract at Cliftonville their priority.

articles.title: Struggling Quins pick up welcome Challenge Cup win
articles.summary: Harlequins shrug off poor form in the Prem to score a half-century of points against French side Vannes.
body: Harlequins put aside their difficulties in the early weeks of the new Prem season to start their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a welcome bonus-point win over French club Vannes.
Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three of their matches, but they were far too strong for their visitors, clocking up nine tries.

England back Marcus Smith contributed 22 points courtesy of two tries and six conversions, while there were two tries from captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans and further efforts from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.
Vannes, who are bottom of the Top 14 with four losses out of four, contributed three tries of their own thanks to Wayan De Benedittis and two from winger Enzo Benmegal.

articles.title: Late tries give Pau bonus-point win over Leicester
articles.summary: Leicester Tigers begin their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau.
body: Portugal international Rodrigo Marta crossed for two of the home side's five tries, with a late burst helping them earn a bonus point from their Pool One opener.
Despite falling behind to an early Pau penalty, Leicester did well in the early exchanges, their tactical kicking game keeping them camped in their opponents' territory.
Billy Searle's 50-22 put the Tigers in superb field position and they capitalised through captain Ollie Chessum, who was making his first appearance of the season after recovering from a foot injury.
Pau fought back well, however, showing their quality with three tries in a 20-minute spell either side of half-time.

articles.title: FSU's loss to Miami may buy Mike Norvell some time, but not free pass
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes broke FSU football's heart, but it may have bought Mike Norvell more time. The Seminoles are still fighting, and that matters.
body: Florida State football walked out of Hard Rock Stadium with another loss Saturday night, but Mike Norvell may have left with something almost as valuable.

The Seminoles' heartbreaking double-overtime defeat to No. 3 Miami did nothing to improve their record, yet it may have altered the conversation surrounding Norvell's future. Instead of looking like a team ready to quit on its coach, FSU fought toe-to-toe with one of the nation's top teams and came within a few plays of pulling off a season-defining upset.
For a coach whose job security has become a weekly topic, that matters.

Some believed Norvell's fate was effectively sealed after last week's loss to Louisville. With FSU struggling through another disappointing season, there were calls for the administration to move on despite a buyout that remains a significant financial hurdle.

articles.title: Chacarra earns third win of year to move top of Race to Dubai standings
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots with the Spaniard's third victory of the season moving him top of the Race to Dubai standings, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, with three events remaining.
body: Chacarra carded a two-under final-round of 70 in New Delhi to reach 21 under as he followed his back-to-back triumphs in June at the KLM Open in Amsterdam and the Italian Open in Turin with another success and secured a fourth DP World Tour title overall having clamed his maiden win at the Hero Indian Open in 2025.

The former LIV player, who took a five-stroke advantage into the final round following a nine-under 63 in round three, picked up shots at two of his first three holes before a bogey at six and then some clutch par putts preceded a birdie at 11.

Pressure was applied by Australia's Daniel Hillier (19 under) - when Hillier birdied the last, Chacarra's advantage was cut to two with three holes remaining - Chacarra's fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo (15 under) and Poland's Adrian Meronk (15 under) but the leader held firm to rise to to 4,092.89 points in the Race to Dubai.

The 26-year-old, who has knocked Reed off top spot for the first time in seven months, could become the third Spaniard, after Jon Rahm (2019) and six-time winner Seve Ballesteros, to be crowned Europe's No 1 golfer.

Can Miami turn around and spark a run coming out of the bye?
According to FanDuel Sportsbook odds, the team is still expected to finish with 4.5 wins this season (-750 on the under).

articles.title: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history
articles.summary: Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.
body: The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.
O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.
Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.
Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

body: Williams scored 16 of her points in the second quarter and no other Valkyries reached double figures as they shot 32.1 per cent and seven of 33 from three-point range.
"We always knew we were going to find a way somehow," Williams said on the microphone postgame as fans chanted "Gabby! Gabby!"
Rhyne Howard missed a three-point attempt with 1:09 left, but Angel Reese made a steal moments later.
Naz Hillmon missed from deep, Kiah Stokes missed the first of two free throws with 23.8 seconds left, and then Allisha Gray missed a three with nine seconds left.
